extracted.intended_audience: general readers and cultural critics interested in race, comedy, and media ethics (also relevant to comedians and writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Stand-up and autobiographical political comedy evaluated for ethical and factual responsibility: guidance about truth-telling, harm to real people, workplace practices, and the broader political consequences of fabricated stories. Focus is on how comedians should handle personal narratives about racism and other harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness in autobiographical storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate or present made-up personal incidents as factual autobiographical events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents multiple fabricated or wildly embellished stories (e.g., drunk woman/Uber driver anecdote; mailed white powder/anthrax story; prom rejection; FBI informant story). It criticizes presenting these fabrications as real and notes that Minhaj admitted some incidents "never actually happened." Anti-patterns: telling invented episodes as true for dramatic effect without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not lie about experiences of racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inventing or exaggerating racist incidents; lying about racism harms racial and ethnic minorities and undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece states, "Lying about racism does a huge disservice to racial and ethnic minorities" and argues fabricated racism stories will "buttress white supremacy" by giving denialists ammunition. Example: fabricated events in specials that claim targeted harassment when records and witnesses show otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent harm to real people (privacy, consent, and doxxing risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care not to expose, identify, or otherwise put real people at risk when telling stories involving them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the alleged prom date whose images were projected (faces blurred only minimally) resulting in "years of harassment and doxing." Guidance: avoid identifying people without consent; do not invite them into productions in ways that lead to harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge embellishment vs. fact (be transparent about fictionality)
rubrics_metrics.description: If material is dramatized, fictionalized, or represents an "emotional truth" rather than literal fact, disclose that to audiences rather than presenting it as straight factual autobiography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minhaj defended fabrications as reflecting "emotional truths," but the article calls that defense intellectually dishonest. Best practice: label composite/fictionalized anecdotes or otherwise make clear you are not asserting factual events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous fact-checking and responsiveness to researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and heed genuine, rigorous fact-checking processes and take seriously staff concerns about factual accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article contrasts claims that the show's fact-checking was "extremely rigorous" with reports that two researchers who challenged material were sidelined. Guidance: listen to and incorporate fact-checkers' findings; do not marginalize or punish staff who raise factual concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge personal privilege and avoid reductive narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: When telling stories about marginalization, acknowledge one's own intersecting privileges and avoid portraying every encounter as simple oppressor/victim binaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes Minhaj omitted context of privilege (education, cultural capital, partial whiteness) and instead "paints a reductive picture of racism" where white people are always aggressors and people of color always victims. Guidance: account for nuance and intersectionality in narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not co-opt others' pain for personal career advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using or appropriating other peoples' suffering or identities as material to advance your career, particularly when those people have less power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article accuses Minhaj of having "co-opted their pain to advance his career," making it "harder for people with less privilege to be believed." Best practice: center and responsibly elevate the actual voices of those affected instead of fabricating their pain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid producing material that empowers denialists or white supremacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that fabricated or exaggerated stories about racism can be weaponized by those who deny systemic racism and therefore must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece argues such lies "will likely only buttress white supremacy" and "vindicate denialists." Guidance: assess the broader political consequences of your narratives; ensure truthfulness to avoid giving fodder to bad-faith actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical caution when implicating individuals or institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful about alleging wrongdoing or sinister motives by named individuals or institutions, since false claims can cause real harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the FBI-informant story that relied on inaccurate chronology and could affect the real person involved; the author says Minhaj was "self-righteously playing god" regarding potential fallout. Guidance: verify claims that could damage reputations before presenting them as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain ethical internal workplace practices (avoid silencing and retaliation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers and showrunners should not foster cultures that marginalize staff, silence dissenting fact-checkers, or tolerate gender discrimination and retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New Yorker reporting referenced alleges three women sued for "gender discrimination, sex-based harassment, and retaliation" and that researchers who challenged material were excluded from meetings. Guidance: ensure equitable workplace procedures, protect those who raise concerns, and address discrimination seriously.
